body:
# Quick Pickles and Brines — Prep Station (Owner: Hannah Becker)

## Scope and Purpose
- Quick, refrigerated pickles for service pans and deli quarts.
- Standardize brine ratios, yields, pH, labeling, cooling, and shelf life.
- Use 5% distilled white vinegar. Keep all product at or below 41°F after cooling.

## Brine Ratios and Batch Specs (Yield: 4 qt finished per recipe)
Short notes: Salt is kosher, fine grain. Spice adds are optional but consistent.

| Item | Cut Spec | Veg Prep Weight | Vinegar (qt) | Water (qt) | Salt (oz) | Sugar (oz) | Spice/Notes | Method |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|---|
| Red Onion | 1/8 in half-moons | 5 lb | 1.25 | 1.25 | 2.5 | 4.0 | 10 peppercorns, 2 bay | Hot pour brine at 180–190°F over onions |
| Cucumber | 1/4 in rounds or spears | 5 lb | 1.25 | 1.25 | 2.25 | 2.0 | 10 dill sprigs, 8 garlic cloves smashed | Cold pack; cool brine to ≤70°F before pour |
| Jalapeño | 1/8 in rings | 4 lb | 1.50 | 1.00 | 2.25 | 1.0 | 1 tsp cumin seed | Hot pour brine at 180–190°F |
| Carrot | 1/8 in bias coins | 5 lb | 1.50 | 1.00 | 2.5 | 3.0 | 1 tsp coriander seed | Blanch carrots 1 min; hot pour brine |

- Above volumes fill 4 x 1-qt deli containers (liquid + veg). If brine seems short, top with same ratio.
- Target pH after 24 hr: ≤4.2. If >4.2, see pH correction below.

## Procedure (All Items)
1) Scale veg, slice to spec; rinse and spin/dry. Pack into clean deli quarts, leaving 1/2 in headspace.
2) Build brine per table. Bring to a bare simmer (180–190°F) to dissolve salt/sugar, then use as called (hot or cooled).
3) For hot-pour: Fill to cover veg; lid loosely 10 minutes to vent, then tighten.
4) For cold-pack: Cool brine to ≤70°F, fill to cover, lid.
5) Cool according to Cooling and Holding table. Do not stack hot containers.
6) Label immediately after packing. Move to walk-in once ≤70°F.
7) Hold refrigerated 24 hours before service for best flavor; verify pH and record.

## Cooling, Holding, Shelf Life
Short notes: Follow FDA Food Code style time/temperature controls.

| Control | Limit/Target | Action |
|---|---|---|
| Brine temp for hot-pour | 180–190°F | Do not boil spices hard; avoid bitterness |
| Cooling (hot items) | 135°F→70°F within 2 hr; 70°F→41°F within 4 hr | Uncovered on sheet pans, single layer; ice bath if needed |
| Cold-holding | ≤41°F | Store on labeled, dedicated pickle shelf |
| Shelf life (refrigerated) | 14 days max from prep | Discard at end of day on discard date |
| pH target | ≤4.2 | Measure at 24 hr; record on label |

## pH Check and Correction
- Meter: Calibrate daily; rinse probe; measure cold sample.
- If pH 4.21–4.39: Add 1–2 fl oz 5% vinegar per qt of brine in container, mix, recheck next day.
- If pH ≥4.40 after adjustment: Discard container and report to Hannah.

## Labeling (Every Container)
Short notes: Use waterproof label on side, not lid.

| Field | What to Write |
|---|---|
| Product | e.g., “Pickled Red Onion” |
| Station/Owner | Prep — Hannah Becker |
| Prep Time | Time of packing (24-hr clock) |
| Discard Date | Prep date + 14 days (end of day) |
| Batch Code | Item initials + today’s service (e.g., RO–PM–A) |
| pH (24 hr) | Numeric reading (e.g., 3.9) |
| Initials | Your initials |

## Service and QC Notes
- Visual: Bright color, clear brine, no slime, no gas or bulging lids. Off odors = discard.
- Always use clean tongs/spoons; no hands in containers. Keep veg submerged.
- Rotate FIFO by batch code. Consolidate only same item, same batch.
summary: Prep station quick pickle SOP: brine ratios, yields, temps, pH ≤4.2, cooling, labeling, and 14-day shelf life. Owner: Hannah Becker.
